items.title: AI tools in recruitment: audit outcomes report
items.why: Source of the quotation (p.3) and the figure (four fifths or 80%, p.21, reported as what providers did, not as a legal standard). Pages 22-23 set out the limits of testing on inferred characteristics and the recommendation to keep test results and report them to senior managers.

items.title: Equality Act 2010, section 19: Indirect discrimination
items.why: The legal question a bias test informs: particular disadvantage, then proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim. The section contains no numerical threshold.

items.title: Guidance on AI and data protection: Annex A, Fairness in the AI lifecycle
items.why: Expects evaluation broken down by group and subgroup, and monitoring after deployment at a frequency proportional to impact. Under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025.

items.title: Guidance on AI and data protection: What about fairness, bias and discrimination?
items.locator: Sections on technical approaches to mitigating discrimination and on processing special category data to assess discrimination
items.why: Confirms special category data may be processed to test performance across groups if an Article 9 condition applies, and calls for ongoing monitoring. Under review; covers data protection only.

items.title: Responsible AI in Recruitment
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.why: Defines bias audit, performance testing and model cards for a buyer, says bias audits should be repeated in operation, and describes model drift.

items.title: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence (Special Publication 1270)
items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (US)
items.locator: PDF pp. 13-14 (legal context, footnote 9) and p. 41 (fairness metrics)
items.why: Traces the four-fifths rule to United States federal employment guidelines (29 C.F.R. 1607.4(D)) and explains why no single fairness metric settles the matter. United States context; not UK law.
